summary: Challis NF lookout: L-4 cab built 1935 in the Frank Church wilderness; last staffed 1997, now on emergency status and in poor shape; reached on foot.

facts.status_note: On emergency status; last staffed 1997. The climbing guide says it was in poor shape and not manned in 2015.

access.note: On emergency status, not staffed since 1997, and described as in poor shape. No source describes public entry into the cabin; ask the Salmon-Challis National Forest before going.

visit.trail_note: Vehicle access on the Sleeping Deer Road (FS-086, 22 miles from the saddle) to within 2 miles of the summit. A signed trail from the road end climbs just over a mile. The Forest Service lists a 0.5-mile trail from the Cabin Creek and Melville Ridge trails. Cellphone service is usually unavailable.

events.note: L-4 cab on the ground, the only structure on the summit per firelookout.com; NHLR calls it a hip-roof L-4 groundhouse with a catwalk.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 9,772 ft (2,979 m); firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 9,881 ft. The record keeps the register figure (2978.5 m). The story reports both.
The register places the lookout in Custer County; firelookout.com places it in Lemhi County. The sources do not settle this, so the story reports both.

The Forest Service page lists a 0.5-mile trail from the Cabin Creek and Melville Ridge trails; the climbing guide describes a signed trail of just over a mile from a saddle near the summit. These may be different routes, and the story reports each.

notes_for_editor: No photos added: the register and Idaho Fire Lookouts credit photos, but the fetched text has no image URLs. The Forest Lookouts page for Sleeping Deer returned 404 and was not used. The Forest Service trail page's title says #4212 while its text says #212; the story does not cite the number. The climbing guide's trail and the Forest Service trail are both reported, not reconciled. Access is restricted because the lookout is on emergency status and in poor shape; no source describes a closure.
